clue.text: Look forward to Bonfire Night with great enthusiasm?

definitions.meaning: to enjoy fires, as anyone keen on a November 5th bonfire does
an idiom for doing something furiously, at full tilt

explanation.walkthrough: Bonfire Night is Britain's November 5th celebration with bonfires and fireworks; the first reading takes the phrase literally as being fond of fires.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means furiously or with tremendous vigour, as in running at top speed.

clue.text: Bishop condemned after one : mass is suppressed

indicators.note: a thing suppressed is held down inside something else, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: after means later
one is the Roman numeral I
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A bishop is sentenced after someone has shut down Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is a newspaper printing artefact and plays no part. Hugh Latimer was an English Protestant bishop burnt at the stake in Oxford in 1555.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Latimer was a Reformation bishop of Worcester condemned and executed as a heretic under Mary I.

clue.text: Bird using pool noisily, having wash

indicators.note: noisily means the word is to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of shared money
the wake is the wash left behind a moving boat

explanation.surface: A seabird splashes loudly in a pond while taking a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small gull of the North Atlantic cliffs, named for its call.

clue.text: Basic health worker never found in Oxford?

definitions.text: Basic health worker never found in Oxford?

parts.words: Basic health worker never found in Oxford?
parts.note: a basic medical aide in rural China; an Oxford is a laced shoe, so someone with bare feet is never found in one, though the city is full of learned doctors

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university city, full of doctors of philosophy, but here it is a style of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The term named rural paramedics trained with basic skills in Maoist China, a primary health worker.

clue.text: Pull a vehicle up during races

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of another

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone tows a car uphill in the middle of a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CART into TRAC, which 'during' puts inside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something towards oneself, as a magnet draws iron, is to exert a pull.

clue.text: Unisex one-piece, not old, specially tailored

indicators.note: a garment specially tailored has been cut and remade, so the letters are rearranged
not means the following letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A one-piece garment for either sex, newly made to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not old' takes one O from ONEPIECE, leaving NEPIECE (or ONEPIECE less an O), which 'specially tailored' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something having characteristics of both sexes or neither, sexless.

clue.text: Little daughter wanted to do some gardening

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small girl was keen to help out in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling unwanted plants from a flowerbed is a typical gardening chore.

clue.text: With energy, bring down game animal

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to land a fish or plane is to bring it down

explanation.surface: A hunter vigorously brings down a quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large African antelope, hunted as big game.

clue.text: Characteristic of some wines producing thirst

definitions.meaning: the quality of a wine lacking sweetness
the parched state of a throat wanting a drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Wines described as sec or brut lack sugar, and a parched mouth is also said to suffer this.

clue.text: Where views may be had that are not worth considering

definitions.meaning: a scene is seen by looking through a glazed opening in a wall
an idiom for something discarded or abandoned, as a plan thrown away

explanation.definitionFit: Ideas tossed aside are said to have been thrown out like rubbish through a casement.

clue.text: Once party of revellers returns, time to get in coach

indicators.note: a piece that gets in goes inside another word
returns means the word is read backwards

parts.note: rout is an archaic word for a noisy party or crowd of revellers

explanation.surface: When the party crowd comes back, it is time to board the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ROUT into TUOR, and 'to get in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to give private teaching, which a private teacher does.

clue.text: It helps create a larger flow of revenue from clients

definitions.text: It helps create a larger flow
definitions.meaning: a stream feeding into a river swells its current
describing payments made by client or vassal states to an overlord

explanation.definitionFit: A river is fed by side streams, and the adjective also means paying tribute.

clue.text: Computer system needing academic, in case

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is an academic
a frame is a case or casing that holds something

explanation.surface: An office computer set-up that requires a scholar to be housed in a cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large central computer serving many terminals.

clue.text: One getting on Cambridge boat failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Goldie is the name of Cambridge University's reserve crew in the Boat Race

explanation.surface: An elderly person climbs aboard a Cambridge rowing boat that won't get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on in years is old, and the informal noun names such a person.

clue.text: Announce extremely rude notice in error

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
out means wrong, as in a calculation that is out

explanation.surface: Someone declares that an offensive sign was posted by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak aloud from a document is to proclaim it to listeners.

clue.text: Middle of 'bend makes severe demands on competitors

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word, without its first and last

parts.note: something that tries you taxes your patience or strength

explanation.surface: A tight bend in the middle of a race taxes the runners.
explanation.definitionFit: Those entered for a race or contest are the competitors in it.

clue.text: Urge liar to reform — resistance : would be unprincipled

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Encouraging a liar to mend their ways, while resisting, would be unethical.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is a printing artefact; 'would be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct that breaks the rules or norms is irregular, lacking proper moral principle.

clue.text: Spare source of loot invested in transmitter

indicators.note: invested in means wrapped inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: a sender transmits a signal

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spare cash from the proceeds of a robbery put into a radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'foot', but the wordplay needs the first letter L, so 'loot' was meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare figure is lean and thin, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Start to sew larger piece of embroidery

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ampler means larger

explanation.surface: A seamstress begins stitching a bigger needlework panel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an embroidered panel showing stitches, letters and mottoes, often a girl's practice work.

clue.text: Salesman' has to add secret ingredient to succeed

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a salesman
to lace a drink is to add something like alcohol secretly

explanation.surface: A salesman must spike something with a hidden extra to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link; 'succeed' means follow on in place of, not do well.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to take over their position, which is to supplant them.

clue.text: Was concerned about foreign article being approved

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another

parts.note: cared means was concerned
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: Someone was anxious about a foreign newspaper piece getting the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cleared has been authorised or given permission.

clue.text: Wage for series of films

definitions.meaning: to wage a war is to conduct or continue it
a long-running British comedy film franchise of broad innuendo

explanation.walkthrough: The British comedy film series began in 1958 with Sergeant and ran to over thirty titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry on a campaign means to conduct it, and the phrase is the title of a series of British film comedies.

clue.text: Drive out quiet, ascetic Muslim

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered or out of place

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Banishing silence, an austere holy man is expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DRIVE into DERVI before SH is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A dervish is a member of a Sufi order who has taken vows of poverty.

clue.text: Red, as 3 introduces himself in passport, pidgin?

parts.note: a speaker introducing himself in pidgin says me, not I
3 refers to the answer at 3 down, whose second word shortens to doc

explanation.surface: A medic introducing himself in broken English, as on his passport, says me doc.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue ('as ... introduces ... in passport, pidgin') sets the pidgin scene: the doctor at 3 down says 'Me doc'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Bordeaux wine region best known for its red claret.

clue.text: Appreciate Italian's figure

parts.note: to dig something is slang for appreciating it
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Admire the Italian's physique.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral from nought to nine is a figure.

clue.text: King, not finishing meat, taking double in soup-bowl

indicators.note: not finishing means the end letter is removed

parts.note: pork is meat
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a ringer is a double or lookalike

explanation.surface: A monarch, leaving his meat unfinished, has a second helping in the bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small shallow bowl with a handle, for porridge or soup.

clue.text: His line involved with a gory disaster?

definitions.text: His line involved with a gory disaster?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier's battle line is caught up in bloody catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' and 'disaster' both mark the mixing of LINE and A GORY; the whole clue also describes the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman foot soldier stood in a battle line, often meeting a bloody end.

clue.text: Directed to turn back horse before I reach the city

indicators.note: to turn back means to reverse direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: led means directed
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: Told to ride a horse back before I arrive in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn back' turns LED into DEL; 'before' and 'reach' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian capital is a city, here defined only loosely.

clue.text: Nasty type taking ecstasy and speed

parts.note: a rat is a nasty, treacherous type
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person on drugs, ecstasy and amphetamine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a pace or velocity, as in a fast rate.

clue.text: Flower brought by husband may show value of thought

parts.note: pennywort is a plant with round leaves

explanation.surface: Flowers bought by a husband may show what he thinks of you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A penny for your thoughts' fixes the worth of a thought at one penny; 'brought by' and 'may show' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount a penny buys is what the saying 'a penny for your thoughts' offers for a notion.
